meta.purpose: Hand-verified verbatim reference set for STT benchmarking across four failure-mode categories.

categories.clean: Clean, low-noise, well-recorded dialogue (little or no music/score/action under speech).
categories.music: Dialogue with music (score, source music, or PA/soundtrack under speech).
categories.noise: Dialogue with environmental / action / crowd noise.

meta.notes: Timecodes are taken from each film's downloaded SRT and are approximate scene boundaries. VERIFY them against YOUR media before clipping; different rips/releases can differ by a few seconds to a few minutes (PAL speedup, intros, logos). Trim to the nearest natural sentence boundary in the audio.

excerpts.scene: Cafe two-hander: Phil buys Rita coffee and a doughnut; 'if you only had one day to live' and Rita's list of her ideal man.
excerpts.why: Cleanest sustained dry two-hander in the set: quiet interior, no music cue, no crowd, natural turn-taking. The low-noise ANCHOR of the calibration scale.

excerpts.scene: Kaffee vs. Jessep climax: 'If you gave an order that Santiago wasn't to be touched...' through 'You can't handle the truth!' and 'You're goddamn right I did!'
excerpts.why: Clean studio courtroom audio but rapid Q&A plus a fast monologue, dense with names, ranks, and legal/military jargon. Tests clean-but-hard: does WER rise on vocabulary alone, absent noise?

excerpts.scene: Opening bar scene: Mark and Erica's rapid-fire date-turned-breakup.
excerpts.why: Densest, fastest, most-overlapping dialogue in the set (~27 cues/min), the canonical Sorkin cross-talk. Pure fast/overlap failure mode with minimal noise, so it isolates speed from music/noise.

excerpts.scene: Fletcher's 'were you rushing or dragging?' chair-throw tirade; band music under tempo corrections, then a speech-dense profane berating.
excerpts.why: Mixes music-under-speech (tempo corrections over the band) with rapid aggressive speech and drum stabs. Tests speech riding over/around live music.

excerpts.scene: Opening 'Harlem Shuffle' coffee run: Baby walks and air-drums; brief barista order.
excerpts.why: Music-DOMINANT with sparse speech. The SRT prints song lyrics as cues, so it also tests the transcriber's (and model's) speech-vs-lyric discrimination. Extreme end of the music axis.

excerpts.scene: Diner meet-cute: Baby and waitress Debora flirt while Carla Thomas 'B-A-B-Y' plays under the whole scene.
excerpts.why: Balanced dialogue-OVER-continuous-music, the everyday version of the music failure mode (vs BD1's music-dominant extreme).

excerpts.scene: Late-night diner two-hander: McCall ('Bob'/'Robert') and Teri/Alina talk over tea; quiet room tone.
excerpts.why: WITHIN-FILM CLEAN CONTROL for The Equalizer. Same film, mics, and cast as EQ4 but with no music. The EQ1 vs EQ4 gap directly tests whether The Equalizer's weakness is film-specific (mix/accents) or condition-specific (dense music-under-speech).

excerpts.scene: Little John / Russians sit-down: overlapping mob crosstalk and threats, then a TV baseball broadcast ('Napoli', 'Holy cow') plays under the room.
excerpts.why: Fast overlapping crosstalk PLUS a media/broadcast bed underneath. Doubles as a noise sample for The Equalizer.

excerpts.scene: Home Mart register robbery: store ambience, raised voices, a tense stick-up over the retail floor.
excerpts.why: Environmental / action noise: big-box store room tone, movement, and shouting over the mix. The noise axis for The Equalizer.

excerpts.scene: Home Mart finale: dialogue over the store PA song while the fight starts ('The song. Which way is it coming from?' / 'The P.A. system's in the security office.').
excerpts.why: The signature DENSE MUSIC-UNDER-SPEECH failure mode this whole set is built to adjudicate, plus action noise. Compare directly against EQ1 (same film, clean).
